note: Recast from the original description of Emerson 1952, in English; the alate and the soldier are both described, with measurement tables (tables 8 and 9). The samples measured for this species are large (28—50 soldiers) and the ranges are actual minimum—maximum values.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The lateral margins of the soldier labrum behind the base of the white median lobe are evenly curved, without or with only the slightest angulation, unlike the labrum of araujoi and triacifer, which has acute lateral corners; the postmentum in lateral view is slightly swollen and curved, its narrowest part from a little more than one half to about two thirds of the widest part; the angle of the notch of the right mandible is about a right angle, whereas in cornutus it is greater than a right angle and in romani about a right angle but the sides of the head are straighter and more parallel and the head thicker (1.62—1.66 mm). Alate tibial spur formula 2:2:2, antenna 13—14 segments.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head brown with pale yellow streaks; fontanelle plate concolorous with the head or slightly paler; postclypeus yellowish brown; pronotum pale yellow or yellowish brown; tibiae and femora pale yellow; wing membrane hyaline, the costa and radius brownish; abdominal tergites the same colour as the palest part of the pronotum, the sternites paler than the tergites. Pronotum with numerous setae and a few short hairs; abdominal tergites with setae in the middle and contrasting short hairs on the sides and posterior margin; sternites with setae and short hairs. Y suture visible. Fontanelle plate slightly projecting above the surface of the head, slightly smaller than or about equal to an ocellus. Compound eyes relatively small, their lower margin about one third of an eye diameter from the lower margin of the head. Ocelli small, slightly shorter and far narrower than the antennal fossae, slightly projecting on the upper side, only about a quarter of their width visible from above, about their own width from the compound eye and less than their own length from it. Postclypeus length about equal to half its width (0.28—0.33:0.54—0.69 mm). Antenna 13—14 segments. Pronotum relatively long, the sides slightly converging posteriorly, the posterior margin slightly to distinctly concave. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Female measurements: head length to the tip of the clypeus 1.56—1.66, head length to the lateral base of the mandibles 1.06—1.12, head width 1.40—1.45, compound eye diameter 0.35—0.38, distance from the compound eye to the lower margin 0.08—0.12, ocellus length 0.17—0.18, width 0.11—0.12, ocellus to compound eye 0.11—0.14, ocellus to fontanelle plate 0.32—0.38, fontanelle plate length 0.12—0.22, width 0.10—0.12, pronotum length 0.65—0.75, width 1.18—1.22, hind tibia length 1.53—1.59, forewing length from the suture 13.44—13.72, width 3.57—3.76 mm (n=4—5); male head width 1.29—1.32, forewing length from the suture 12.34—12.87, width 3.29—3.66 mm (n=4). Compared with araujoi, the mid-tibia of the latter is dark and contrasts clearly with the pale yellow femora and tarsi, and its body is larger; compared with striatus, the latter has 15 antennal segments, a tibial spur formula of 3:2:2 and a larger body.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Vertex with sparse scattered setae, the underside of the head near the postmentum without setae; anterior end of the postmentum with a few setae, its surface with extremely fine hairs. Head somewhat rectangular or nearly oval, the sides slightly to distinctly curved, nearly parallel or slightly converging anteriorly. Frontal tube fairly long, extending distinctly beyond the base of the postclypeus from above. Postmentum in lateral view slightly swollen and curved, its narrowest part from a little more than one half to about two thirds of the widest part. Antenna 14 segments. Lateral margins of the labrum behind the base of the median lobe evenly curved, without or with only the slightest angulation. Mandibles as in figure 2B and figure 11. Anterior margin of the pronotum concave or not. Tibial spur formula 2:2:2. Measurements: head including mandibles 2.41—3.38, head length to the tip of the frontal tube 1.82—2.35, head length to the lateral base of the mandibles 1.70—2.44, head width 1.35—1.71, head thickness 1.22—1.53, frontal tube length 0.31—0.53, labrum width 0.45—0.54, left mandible length 1.04—1.26, right mandible length from the notch 0.57—0.67, pronotum length 0.44—0.68, width 0.73—0.94, hind tibia length 1.18—1.48 mm (n=28—50). Type locality Itajaí, Santa Catarina, Brazil (27°10′S, 48°48′W), collected and identified by Fr. Müller.
